title: Asking Jayden Daniels about the cease-and-desist absolutely matters and absolutely needed to be asked. People should be afforded the chance to speak and not simply have court filings and letters drawn up by lawyers tell the story. Those filings don’t capture the emotional element and the ‘why’ behind the action. He could have used this to speak on what that number means to him and possibly won back some folks in the court of public opinion after they’ve memed him to oblivion. Sometimes people decline to speak any further for legal reasons — and that’s totally their right — he politely did that. But you still afford them the opportunity. That’s being a fair journalist.

title: Notes from today's practice as I review my notes: • If the opener was tomorrow, I think Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome would be the starting corners. If Banks gets the start, he will have earned it. But that would mean a matchup against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens right out of the gate ... so I'd let the competition continue to give Paulson Adebo a chance to make up ground. He has picked it up after a slow start to camp. • I have covered 11 camps now, but somehow can still get tunnel vision in the early days. But the cream usually rises to the top with proven NFL players stepping up and unknowns who flash fizzling out. Should learn that lesson by now. This pertains to Darnell Mooney, who has turned it on as the season has drawn closer. I'll make him the early favorite to step into Calvin Austin's role alongside Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields in 11 personnel. Braxton Berrios will also have an opportunity to push for slot snaps. • The front seven has tipped an excessive amount of passes this summer. It seems like Brian Burns gets one per day. • The kicking competition was spiced up by some extra long attempts today as the rest of the team urged them to keep backing up. The longest attempts were from 69 yards. Both kickers missed from there, but each connected from 60+. Dominic Zvada went 8-for-10 and Ben Sauls went 7-for-10, which is actually impressive considering how many of the kicks were from 50+. I don't see any way Zvada doesn't win the competition. • The tightest position battle heading into the preseason finale is backup center. Lucas Patrick was first up with the second-team offense, but he alternated with Bryan Hudson. You can make a case to keep either or even both. They have the most on the line on Friday night.

But that would mean a matchup against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens right out of the gate ... so I'd let the competition continue to give Paulson Adebo a chance to make up ground. He has picked it up after a slow start to camp. 

• I have covered 11 camps now, but somehow can still get tunnel vision in the early days. But the cream usually rises to the top with proven NFL players stepping up and unknowns who flash fizzling out. Should learn that lesson by now.

This pertains to Darnell Mooney, who has turned it on as the season has drawn closer. I'll make him the early favorite to step into Calvin Austin's role alongside Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields in 11 personnel. 

Braxton Berrios will also have an opportunity to push for slot snaps. 

• The front seven has tipped an excessive amount of passes this summer. It seems like Brian Burns gets one per day. 

• The kicking competition was spiced up by some extra long attempts today as the rest of the team urged them to keep backing up. The longest attempts were from 69 yards. Both kickers missed from there, but each connected from 60+.

Dominic Zvada went 8-for-10 and Ben Sauls went 7-for-10, which is actually impressive considering how many of the kicks were from 50+. I don't see any way Zvada doesn't win the competition.

title: Roger Goodell on the Pro Bowl changes: “I think we’ve been focused on the game. You’ve heard me say it for many years about the quality of the game in the Pro Bowl. I don’t think it’s up to NFL standards. And that’s why we changed to the flag game several years ago. So I’m not sure the last time you want to say we played a game in a football sense. "So I think this is something that we talked to our players about, the Pro Bowl players in particular. We had conference calls the last couple years: What’s working? What’s not? What would you like to see? And the number one thing that came out—and there were a lot of wonderful comments by the players—one is: ‘We want to be honored and celebrated as a Pro Bowl player.’… It just opened my eyes. I never really thought about it in the context of that. It’s not honoring the replacement players. It’s honoring the guys who are selected by the fans, by the players, by the coaches. "And so that was really the core of it, is: How do we do this in the right way? And our players, you know, they did what they normally do. They had great recommendations on how to do that. And second, a willingness to lead that the all-star format doesn’t really work for our game…. It’s something that we felt strongly about. And I think our players, they deserve to be celebrated when they get the Pro Bowl honor.”

title: A few observations from watching #Texans and #Panthers joint practice with a legend: - Physical practice from both teams. It works out well when teams practice with the same style and aggression as opposed to the teams having different approaches toward practice. Probably why there weren't any fights to be honest. - The Texans defense didn't allow Bryce Young much time at all. A number of dropbacks were would be sacks, and it wasn't just from the outside with Anderson and Hunter. (Hunter was incredible today) - Houston's secondary was STICKY. S Calen Bullock (who should be more well know around the league) picked Young 2x. - Jimmy Horn Jr. who has had a good camp, put on some weight, had the play of the day for the Panthers. He went up and caught a TD over the middle in tight coverage and held onto the contested catch. It was the final play of practice. - Stroud looks in more control at the LOS. He's making all the calls and setting the protections. You can see he's growing with Caley. - Kayshon Boutte was in pads, but working on the side. The Texans are acclimating him the right way and taking their time. The heat is actually a factor in this. Stroud I know likes Boutte. - David Montgomery is just a good football player. He'll change this offense. - It's fun seeing Jayce Horn in the slot. Not sure how much it's used this year, but he's such a good blitzer. - Texans OL is starting to gel. You could tell today. - I watched practice with my man @SteveSmithSr89 He loves Jonathan Brooks and thinks he changes this offense. To be more specific, loved how Brooks lowered his shoulder on a run before going out of bounds. A good sign he feels comfortable with his knee.

- Houston's secondary was STICKY. S Calen Bullock (who should be more well know around the league) picked Young 2x.
- Jimmy Horn Jr. who has had a good camp, put on some weight, had the play of the day for the Panthers. He went up and caught a TD over the middle in tight coverage and held onto the contested catch. It was the final play of practice.
